title: Adaptive blockwise requantification and kernel heuristics for streaming prefill
creator: Samira Patel
description:
Problem: Streaming and long-context workloads pay an asymmetric cost from dequantization and precision transitions. Current kernel selector often triggers full dequant/requant cycles at microbatch boundaries which inflates per-token latency and spend for INT8/FP8 mixed-precision paths.

Goal: Implement an adaptive blockwise requantification strategy plus a lightweight kernel heuristic that: (1) minimizes unnecessary dequant/requant transitions across contiguous token windows, (2) prefers integer-friendly kernels for short on-device attention when quality risk is low, and (3) exposes safe runtime knobs for canarying on Dedicated/Hosted. The feature should reduce per-token cost on streaming decode workloads and maintain model output quality within our regression SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end p95 latency regression <= 3% vs baseline on streaming decode workloads (seq_len 2048, batch 1)
Tokenized inference cost reduction >= 12% on representative streaming traces (measured across 5 customers/benchmarks)
Quality regressions < 1% on the curated streaming prompt eval suite (LLM-eval: next-token accuracy / token-level perplexity), with per-model opt-out if risk detected
Automated fallback to FP16/FP32 path when observed dequant jitter or soft-failure rate exceeds threshold
Instrumentation surfaced in Console: per-route dequant-count, blockwise-requant decisions, p95 delta and cost delta visible in rollout dashboard
implementation_notes: Introduce 'block_score' in kernel selector: block_score = alpha * latency_est + beta * dequant_cost + gamma * quality_risk; coefficients configurable per customer tier
Define block boundary heuristics: prefer grouping prefill tokens into adaptive blocks (size determined by moving average of recent token latencies and cache hit rate)

Optimistic integer path: allow in-place INT8 attention kernels to execute without full dequant when headwise-scale variance < threshold; add quick runtime guard to validate numerical drift on sampled tokens
Requant path: opportunistic requant at microbatch merge points instead of every prefill/decoding transition; add counters to avoid repeated toggles for the same sequence window
Telemetry: add sampling of numeric deltas (int vs fp) and a low-overhead 'shadow run' mode to calibrate quality_risk per model/version
Unit/Integration tests: microbench harness for prefills with variable cache-hit %, mock long-context streams, golden outputs for drift detection
Performance harness: add 1) token-level flame graphs, 2) synthetic streaming traces (seq_len 512/1024/2048) and 3) multi-GPU routing scenarios for Dedicated
Fallback strategy: explicit policy chain - prefer quant-kernel -> if soft-fail increase confidence score -> if repeated failures escalate to fp-path and tag model as 'quant-risk' for 24h

2026-03-06: Internal review notes from runtime team: need tighter probe budget on shadow runs to keep overhead <1% and add canary flag for enterprise tenants
2026-03-10: Perf tests across A100 and T4 show variable gains (A100: ~11% token cost reduction, T4: ~18%); added model-specific confidence gating to address regression risk
